# Mutants the tests miss on macOS, each with the reason it cannot change
# behavior there. The `mutants` workflow fails when the mutants it misses
# differ from this list. A line is a mutant as `cargo mutants --list` names
# it, without its line and column, so a name that occurs twice in a file is
# listed once for each miss.

# macOS has no Landlock, so `lock` intersects the requested restrictions with
# an empty set and never reads the result. Linux runs the tests that need it.
crates/fsgate/src/lib.rs: replace | with & in LockOptions::requested
crates/fsgate/src/lib.rs: replace | with ^ in LockOptions::requested

# `CAN_READ_PEER_UID` is true on Linux and macOS, so the guard is false
# without the mutant too. It matters only where fsgate cannot read a peer's
# uid, which no CI runner is.
crates/fsgate/src/broker.rs: replace match guard !CAN_READ_PEER_UID with false in ServeOptions::allowed_uids

# Not built on macOS: the Linux `apply`. The macOS `apply` has a mutant of
# the same name, which the tests catch, and so the workflow cannot leave this
# one out without a line number.
crates/fsgate/src/containment.rs: replace apply -> Result<Applied, GateError> with Ok(Default::default())
crates/fsgate/src/containment.rs: replace == with != in apply
